traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Apocynaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves simple, lamina entire (not cut); Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): leaves simple.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Lucid family key, Apocynaceae (read 2026-10-17): simple symmetric blades, linear, lanceolate, ovate, elliptic, oblanceolate, oblong or orbicular, bases sometimes cordate or lobed. Ranking ours, by genus size: the woody genera (Tabernaemontana, Rauvolfia, Alstonia) and Hoya are mostly elliptic; ovate to heart-shaped blades in many twining milkweeds (Cynanchum, Marsdenia); narrow in Asclepias.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 406, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 233 Apocynaceae, 234 Periplocaceae and 235 Asclepiadaceae (orders Apocynales), which APG joins as Apocynaceae: trees, shrubs, climbers and twiners, less often herbs; leaves opposite or whorled, rarely alternate, simple, entire; no stipules; flowers regular, bisexual, the calyx lobes 5 (rarely 4), the corolla united; stamens 5 (rarely 4) on the corolla tube; two carpels, often free or parting in fruit; ovary superior; the milkweeds' flowers mostly in cymes; fruit a pair of follicles in most, a berry or drupe in some. The follicle is read as usual from the milkweeds and from the order's 'carpels 2, often free, or becoming free in fruit'.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Apocynaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Asclepiadaceae, Plocospermataceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded evergreen. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
